clue.text: Little power and energy in standard conference presentation

indicators.note: in says the two small pieces sit inside the word for standard

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in 'up to par'
P is the short form of power, the little version of the word
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A small amount of power and energy is all you get from the usual talk at a conference.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper is a talk or study read out to delegates at an academic meeting.

clue.text: Anthropomorphism? It's not much of a deception

parts.note: pathetic means feeble, not much good
a fallacy is a false idea, a deception

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses treating animals as human as a feeble trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: the term covers giving human feelings to nature or weather, close to anthropomorphism.
explanation.definitionFit: The literary term means attributing human emotions to inanimate things, like a 'cruel sea'.

clue.text: Softly illuminated fringe for a hairstyle

parts.note: p is piano, softly in music

indicators.note: fringe means border, so the word for illuminated surrounds the A

parts.note: lit means illuminated

explanation.surface: A gently lit fringe for a hair-do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringe' suggests a haircut but is the container signal: LIT edges A.
explanation.definitionFit: A plait is hair braided into strands.

clue.text: Strange sort occupying strange platform

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the mixed-up letters go into the other word

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: Strange says the letters of sort are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd character occupies a peculiar stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'strange's do different jobs: the first, 'Strange', is the anagram signal for 'sort', the second is RUM, old British slang for odd, which 'occupying' says the jumbled letters go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand for a speaker.

clue.text: Was I not ab? Wrong — I was

definitions.text: Was I not ab? Wrong — I was

indicators.note: Wrong says the letters of the preceding words are set out wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor protests that he was not an able seaman, then corrects himself: he was.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is an able seaman; a ship's petty officer in charge of rigging has usually risen from that rank, so the speaker, now in charge, once was an AB. The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun is the ship's officer in charge of deck crew, typically promoted from among the able seamen.

clue.text: Drink, improved, shunned by non-drinker

indicators.note: shunned by says the letters for the non-drinker are kept out of the word

parts.note: better means improved
TT is teetotal, someone who never drinks alcohol

explanation.surface: An improved drink is spurned by a teetotaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is an alcoholic beverage brewed from malt and hops.

clue.text: Town's dubious Latin charm

indicators.note: dubious says the letters of Latin charm are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A town's appeal is a doubtful Latin charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Altrincham is a market town in Greater Manchester, formerly Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This place in north-west England is a market town near Manchester.

clue.text: Broke up most of aggregate in outhouse

indicators.note: in says the shortened piece sits inside the word for outhouse

parts.note: a shed is a small outbuilding

indicators.note: most of means drop the final letter

parts.note: a mass is a collected whole, an aggregate

explanation.surface: Someone broke up most of the gravel in the shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke up' reads like a past-tense verb for a crowd dispersing, but it means shattered; 'most of' drops the last letter of the word for aggregate before 'in' puts it in the shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed means shattered, broken to pieces.

clue.text: Area currently affected by global warming?

definitions.text: Area currently affected by global warming?

parts.words: Area currently affected by global warming
parts.note: sounds like climate change, but means the part of the globe being warmed by summer now, in the northern winter

explanation.walkthrough: When Britain shivers in winter, the summer sun warms the southern hemisphere, notably this continent.
explanation.definitionFit: This continent lies in the southern hemisphere, so it has summer during the British winter.

clue.text: There's a place for public hanging in Trafalgar square

definitions.text: There's a place for public hanging in Trafalgar square

parts.words: There's a place for public hanging in Trafalgar square
parts.note: suggests executions, but the hanging is of pictures, in a public gallery on Trafalgar Square in London

explanation.walkthrough: Trafalgar Square is in central London; the hanging is of paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: The national art collection in London is housed on the north side of Trafalgar Square.

clue.text: Doll one's playing with?

parts.note: reads like a child with a toy, but means the Shakespeare character Doll, of Henry IV Part 2, whom a stage actor plays opposite

explanation.walkthrough: Doll is not a toy but the tavern prostitute in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2, whose surname is the answer; the actor playing Falstaff is 'playing with' her.
explanation.definitionFit: Doll's surname in Shakespeare's history play gives this Eastcheap character her full stage name.

clue.text: A benefit when fixed?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left, it rained'
set means fixed or settled, as a set date

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a perk becomes valuable once it is arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'when fixed' as AS SET: 'as' for 'when', 'set' for 'fixed'.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, something that brings advantage.

clue.text: Powerless suppressed rage covering everything

indicators.note: Powerless tells us to drop the letter for power, P, from the word that follows

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means held in or suppressed
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: A helpless person's bottled-up fury spreads over everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole, complete, taking in every part.

clue.text: Previously a chart-topper with other arrangement

parts.note: a hit is a successful record, one that tops the charts

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters of the next word are set in a new order, as a musical arrangement reworks a tune

explanation.surface: A number one single is re-recorded in a different arrangement from before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a chart-topper' suggests a pop record or a number one, which is right: a hit. 'arrangement' is the anagram signal, borrowed from music, acting on 'other'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto means up to now, until this time.

clue.text: Somehow get mica to one sculptor

indicators.note: Somehow says the letters of the next words fall into place in some new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Somehow you must get the mineral mica to an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges GET MICA TO to GIACOMETT, then I is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberto Giacometti was a Swiss artist famed for thin elongated figures in bronze.

clue.text: Someone having problems getting out?

parts.note: sounds like a prisoner or someone stuck in a room, but 'getting out' is dropping off to sleep, going out like a light

explanation.walkthrough: 'getting out' suggests escape; here it means losing consciousness, so the person cannot sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sufferer from sleeplessness has trouble falling asleep at night.

clue.text: One who's wrong to take the money and run?

definitions.text: One who's wrong to take the money and run?

parts.words: One who's wrong to take the money and run
parts.note: sounds like a thief, but describes a supposed amateur athlete secretly paid to compete in races

explanation.walkthrough: A nominal amateur sportsman who accepts payment breaks the rules of amateur sport; 'run' means a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for a fake amateur covers a sportsperson who secretly takes payment.

clue.text: Letter was primary in returning thanks

indicators.note: returning means the word for was primary is read backwards

parts.note: led means went first, was primary
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A letter of thanks was the first to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns LED into DEL; TA is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Weak opening to fable story-teller rejected

indicators.note: opening to says take the first letter of fable
rejected means the word for story-teller is turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: a liar tells stories, untrue ones

explanation.surface: A poor beginning to a fable makes the author turn it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story-teller' looks like the author of the fable, but it is a liar; 'rejected' sends that word backwards, giving a word for railing.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail means delicate and feeble, lacking strength.

clue.text: Architect working in un style?

indicators.note: working says the letters of un style are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: An architect working in an un-stylish manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edwin Lutyens designed much of New Delhi and the Cenotaph in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin Lutyens was a leading British architect of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Working hard, they're linked for some time

definitions.text: Working hard, they're linked for some time

parts.words: Working hard, they're linked for some time
parts.note: sounds like close colleagues, but describes convicts shackled together doing hard labour while serving their time

explanation.walkthrough: 'for some time' hints at a prison sentence; 'linked' is literal, by chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a group of prisoners is chained together while doing hard labour outside the jail.

clue.text: Impartial report of recent court case one's thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out says the letter for one is removed
report of says the phrase is spoken, giving letters by sound

parts.note: a new trial is a recent court case
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unbiased account of a recent court case that was dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'new trial' gives NEUTRIAL; 'thrown out' removes the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral means taking no side in a dispute.

clue.text: Pass sentence, given period of preparation

parts.note: to lead a life is to pass it, as in 'lead a quiet life'
time is a prison sentence, as in 'doing time'

explanation.surface: A judge hands down a sentence after a period to get ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead time is the interval needed between starting a task and its completion or delivery.

clue.text: Has to cut odd bits of shell, served seafood

indicators.note: cut says the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: must means has to

indicators.note: odd bits of says take the first, third and fifth letters of shell

explanation.surface: Someone must crack bits of shell off before serving fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims MUST to MUS; 'odd bits of' shell are S, E, L.
explanation.definitionFit: This bivalve is a shellfish often served steamed, so a kind of seafood.

clue.text: Drudge apppears to look hungry, but not finishing

indicators.note: not finishing says drop the last letter

parts.note: to slaver is to drool, as a hungry animal does

explanation.surface: A drudge seems to look starved, but not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' drops the final R of SLAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave is someone forced to do hard, menial work.

clue.text: Element in boardrooms knocking the city

indicators.note: Element in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the boardroom criticism is aimed at the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the city' looks like London's financial district; it is a Siberian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large city in south-western Siberia, Russia.

clue.text: Direction to strike out, pursuing a girl

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this piece follows A

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's instruction to delete

explanation.surface: A proofreader's mark to remove something is chasing a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: DELE is Latin for 'delete', a proof-correction mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Fighter of legend taking the quieter route?

parts.note: tamer means more docile, quieter
a lane is a small road or route

explanation.surface: A legendary warrior chooses the less dangerous path.
explanation.definitionFit: Timur, the fourteenth-century Central Asian conqueror, is known in English legend and drama by this name.

clue.text: Measure the credit of London police?

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police; 'of' makes it possessive
tick is British slang for credit, buying 'on tick'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the Met's credit rating is.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is London police headquarters; 'on tick' means on credit in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard against which things are judged.

clue.text: Wary swimmer turns back, encountering lines

indicators.note: turns back means the word for swimmer is read in reverse

parts.note: an eel is a swimming fish
RY is short for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A nervous swimmer turns back on meeting the lane ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns back' makes LEE from EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Leery means suspicious or cautious.
